functions.name: WasmEdge_ModuleInstanceDelete
functions.description: Destroy a module instance. If registered into one or more store contexts, it is automatically unregistered. Do not use the context after deletion.
requirements: Cxt must be a module instance previously created; after deletion, it must not be used.
If the module has been registered in stores, it will be unregistered automatically.

functions.name: WasmEdge_FunctionInstanceCreate
functions.signature: WASMEDGE_CAPI_EXPORT extern WasmEdge_FunctionInstanceContext * WasmEdge_FunctionInstanceCreate(const WasmEdge_FunctionTypeContext *Type, WasmEdge_HostFunc_t HostFunc, void *Data, const uint64_t Cost);
functions.description: Create a host function instance with a concrete function type and a C host function pointer. The Data pointer is stored with the instance. The instance is typically added to a module for export.
requirements: Type must describe the exact parameter/result types expected by HostFunc; Params and Returns lengths are guaranteed to match Type during invocation.
HostFunc must match WasmEdge_HostFunc_t signature and return a WasmEdge_Result status.
Data may be NULL; the caller must ensure its lifetime while the function exists.
Cost is the function cost for statistics; pass 0 if not needed.
On success, the caller owns the instance and must delete it with WasmEdge_FunctionInstanceDelete unless it is added to a module (ownership transferred).
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check for NULL.

functions.name: WasmEdge_FunctionInstanceCreateBinding
functions.signature: WASMEDGE_CAPI_EXPORT extern WasmEdge_FunctionInstanceContext * WasmEdge_FunctionInstanceCreateBinding(const WasmEdge_FunctionTypeContext *Type, WasmEdge_WrapFunc_t WrapFunc, void *Binding, void *Data, const uint64_t Cost);
functions.description: Create a host function instance using a wrapper function suitable for languages that cannot pass a direct function pointer. The Binding is provided as the first argument (This) to the wrapper when invoked.
requirements: Type must match the wrapper’s effective parameter/result types; ParamLen and ReturnLen at invocation time match Type.
WrapFunc must match WasmEdge_WrapFunc_t signature and return a WasmEdge_Result.
Binding is passed as the This argument to WrapFunc when invoked; may represent a foreign function reference.
Data may be NULL; caller must ensure Data lifetime.
Cost is for statistics; pass 0 if not needed.
On success, caller must delete with WasmEdge_FunctionInstanceDelete unless ownership is transferred to a module.
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check for NULL.

functions.name: WasmEdge_FunctionInstanceGetData
functions.signature: WASMEDGE_CAPI_EXPORT extern const void * WasmEdge_FunctionInstanceGetData(const WasmEdge_FunctionInstanceContext *Cxt);
functions.description: Get the Data pointer associated with a function instance (as provided during creation).
requirements: Cxt must be a valid function instance context.
Returns NULL on failure; callers must handle NULL.
Returned pointer is const; actual object lifetime is managed externally by the creator.

functions.name: WasmEdge_FunctionInstanceGetFunctionType
functions.description: Retrieve the function type context for a function instance. The returned type context is owned by the function instance and must not be deleted by the caller.
requirements: Cxt must be valid.
Caller must NOT call WasmEdge_FunctionTypeDelete on the returned pointer.
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check for NULL.

functions.name: WasmEdge_FunctionInstanceDelete
functions.description: Destroy a function instance. Do not use the context after deletion.
requirements: Cxt must not be used after deletion.
If the instance has been added to a module, the caller must NOT delete it (ownership transferred).

functions.name: WasmEdge_TableInstanceCreate
functions.description: Create a table instance from a table type. When the table grows, new elements default to null references of the table type’s reference type. For non-nullable reference types, use CreateWithInit instead.
requirements: TabType must be a valid table type context.
If the table’s reference type is non-nullable, this API is not suitable; use WasmEdge_TableInstanceCreateWithInit.
Caller owns the instance until added to a module; must delete with WasmEdge_TableInstanceDelete if not added.
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check for NULL.

functions.name: WasmEdge_TableInstanceCreateWithInit
functions.signature: WASMEDGE_CAPI_EXPORT extern WasmEdge_TableInstanceContext * WasmEdge_TableInstanceCreateWithInit(const WasmEdge_TableTypeContext *TabType, const WasmEdge_Value Value);
functions.description: Create a table instance with a non-null default init value for elements when the table grows. The value must be type-compatible with the table’s reference type and non-null for non-nullable reference types.
requirements: TabType must be valid.
Value must be compatible with the table type’s reference type; for non-nullable reference types, Value must be non-null or creation fails.
Caller owns the instance until added to a module; must delete with WasmEdge_TableInstanceDelete if not added.
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check for NULL.

functions.name: WasmEdge_TableInstanceGetTableType
functions.signature: WASMEDGE_CAPI_EXPORT extern const WasmEdge_TableTypeContext * WasmEdge_TableInstanceGetTableType(const WasmEdge_TableInstanceContext *Cxt);
functions.description: Get the table type from a table instance. Returned type is owned by the instance; do not delete it.
requirements: Cxt must be valid.
Caller must NOT call WasmEdge_TableTypeDelete on the returned pointer.
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check for NULL.

functions.name: WasmEdge_TableInstanceGetData
functions.signature: WASMEDGE_CAPI_EXPORT extern WasmEdge_Result WasmEdge_TableInstanceGetData(const WasmEdge_TableInstanceContext *Cxt, WasmEdge_Value *Data, const uint32_t Offset);
functions.description: Read a reference value at the given index from a table instance into Data.
requirements: Cxt must be valid.
Data must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the value.
Offset must be within the current table size; otherwise the function fails.
Callers must check the returned WasmEdge_Result and may use WasmEdge_ResultGetMessage for error details.

functions.name: WasmEdge_TableInstanceSetData
functions.signature: WASMEDGE_CAPI_EXPORT extern WasmEdge_Result WasmEdge_TableInstanceSetData(WasmEdge_TableInstanceContext *Cxt, WasmEdge_Value Data, const uint32_t Offset);
functions.description: Set a reference value at the given index in a table instance.
requirements: Cxt must be valid and mutable.
Data’s type must be compatible with the table’s reference type and nullability rules.
Offset must be within the current table size; otherwise the function fails.
Callers must check the returned WasmEdge_Result for success or error.

functions.name: WasmEdge_TableInstanceGetSize
functions.description: Get the current number of elements in the table instance.
requirements: Cxt must be valid.

functions.name: WasmEdge_TableInstanceGrow
functions.signature: WASMEDGE_CAPI_EXPORT extern WasmEdge_Result WasmEdge_TableInstanceGrow(WasmEdge_TableInstanceContext *Cxt, const uint32_t Size);
functions.description: Grow the table instance by Size elements, initializing new entries with the table’s default init value (null or the value provided at creation).
requirements: Cxt must be valid and growable according to its limits.
Size is the number of additional elements to add; must not exceed maximum limits or growth fails.
Callers must check the returned WasmEdge_Result for success or error.

functions.name: WasmEdge_TableInstanceDelete
functions.description: Destroy a table instance. Do not use the context after deletion.
requirements: If the table has been added to a module (ownership transferred), the caller must NOT delete it.
Cxt must not be used after deletion.

functions.name: WasmEdge_MemoryInstanceCreate
functions.description: Create a memory instance from a memory type context.
requirements: MemType must be a valid memory type context.
Caller owns the instance until added to a module; must delete with WasmEdge_MemoryInstanceDelete if not added.
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check for NULL.

functions.name: WasmEdge_MemoryInstanceGetMemoryType
functions.description: Get the memory type context from a memory instance. Returned type is owned by the instance; do not delete it.
requirements: Cxt must be valid.
Caller must NOT call WasmEdge_MemoryTypeDelete on the returned pointer.
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check for NULL.

functions.name: WasmEdge_MemoryInstanceGetData
functions.signature: WASMEDGE_CAPI_EXPORT extern WasmEdge_Result WasmEdge_MemoryInstanceGetData(const WasmEdge_MemoryInstanceContext *Cxt, uint8_t *Data, const uint32_t Offset, const uint32_t Length);
functions.description: Copy data out of a memory instance into the provided buffer starting at Offset for Length bytes.
requirements: Cxt must be valid.
Data must point to a writable buffer of at least Length bytes.
Offset + Length must be within the current memory size; otherwise the function fails.
Callers must check the returned WasmEdge_Result and may use WasmEdge_ResultGetMessage for error details.

functions.name: WasmEdge_MemoryInstanceSetData
functions.signature: WASMEDGE_CAPI_EXPORT extern WasmEdge_Result WasmEdge_MemoryInstanceSetData(WasmEdge_MemoryInstanceContext *Cxt, const uint8_t *Data, const uint32_t Offset, const uint32_t Length);
functions.description: Copy data from the provided buffer into the memory instance starting at Offset for Length bytes.
requirements: Cxt must be valid.
Data must point to a readable buffer of at least Length bytes.
Offset + Length must be within the current memory size; otherwise the function fails.
Callers must check the returned WasmEdge_Result for success or error.

functions.name: WasmEdge_MemoryInstanceGetPointer
functions.signature: WASMEDGE_CAPI_EXPORT extern uint8_t * WasmEdge_MemoryInstanceGetPointer(WasmEdge_MemoryInstanceContext *Cxt, const uint32_t Offset, const uint32_t Length);
functions.description: Obtain a direct writable pointer into the memory instance at Offset for Length bytes. Returns NULL if the requested range is out of bounds.
requirements: Cxt must be valid.
Offset + Length must be within the current memory size; otherwise NULL is returned.
Returned pointer is only valid while the memory instance remains valid and unmoved; callers must not use it after instance deletion or reallocation events.

functions.name: WasmEdge_MemoryInstanceGetPointerConst
functions.signature: WASMEDGE_CAPI_EXPORT extern const uint8_t * WasmEdge_MemoryInstanceGetPointerConst(const WasmEdge_MemoryInstanceContext *Cxt, const uint32_t Offset, const uint32_t Length);
functions.description: Obtain a direct read-only pointer into the memory instance at Offset for Length bytes. Returns NULL if the requested range is out of bounds.
requirements: Cxt must be valid.
Offset + Length must be within bounds; otherwise NULL is returned.
Pointer is tied to the memory instance lifetime.

functions.name: WasmEdge_MemoryInstanceGetPageSize
functions.description: Get the current page size (pages of 64 KiB) of the memory instance.
requirements: Cxt must be valid.

functions.name: WasmEdge_MemoryInstanceGrowPage
functions.signature: WASMEDGE_CAPI_EXPORT extern WasmEdge_Result WasmEdge_MemoryInstanceGrowPage(WasmEdge_MemoryInstanceContext *Cxt, const uint32_t Page);
functions.description: Grow the memory instance by the specified number of pages (each 64 KiB).
requirements: Cxt must be valid and growable according to its limits.
Page is the number of pages to add; growth fails if it would exceed the maximum.
Callers must check the returned WasmEdge_Result.

functions.name: WasmEdge_MemoryInstanceDelete
functions.description: Destroy a memory instance. Do not use the context after deletion.
requirements: If the memory has been added to a module (ownership transferred), the caller must NOT delete it.
Cxt must not be used after deletion.

functions.name: WasmEdge_TagInstanceGetTagType
functions.signature: WASMEDGE_CAPI_EXPORT extern const WasmEdge_TagTypeContext * WasmEdge_TagInstanceGetTagType(const WasmEdge_TagInstanceContext *Cxt);
functions.description: Get the tag type context from a tag instance. The returned type context is owned by the instance.
requirements: Cxt must be valid.
Caller must not delete the returned type context.
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check for NULL.

functions.name: WasmEdge_GlobalInstanceCreate
functions.signature: WASMEDGE_CAPI_EXPORT extern WasmEdge_GlobalInstanceContext * WasmEdge_GlobalInstanceCreate(const WasmEdge_GlobalTypeContext *GlobType, const WasmEdge_Value Value);
functions.description: Create a global instance with the given type and initial value. Fails if the type of Value does not match the global type.
requirements: GlobType must be a valid global type context.
Value must have the same value type as required by GlobType; otherwise creation fails.
Caller owns the instance until added to a module; must delete with WasmEdge_GlobalInstanceDelete if not added.
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check for NULL.

functions.name: WasmEdge_GlobalInstanceGetGlobalType
functions.description: Get the global type context from a global instance. Returned type is owned by the instance; do not delete it.
requirements: Cxt must be valid.
Caller must NOT call WasmEdge_GlobalTypeDelete on the returned pointer.
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check for NULL.

functions.name: WasmEdge_GlobalInstanceGetValue
functions.description: Get the current value of a global instance.
requirements: Cxt must be valid.

functions.name: WasmEdge_GlobalInstanceSetValue
functions.signature: WASMEDGE_CAPI_EXPORT extern WasmEdge_Result WasmEdge_GlobalInstanceSetValue(WasmEdge_GlobalInstanceContext *Cxt, const WasmEdge_Value Value);
functions.description: Set the value of a global instance. Fails if the global is const (immutable) or if the value type does not match.
requirements: Cxt must be valid and the global must be mutable (not Const).
Value type must match the global’s value type.
Callers must check the returned WasmEdge_Result for success or error.

functions.name: WasmEdge_GlobalInstanceDelete
functions.description: Destroy a global instance. Do not use the context after deletion.
requirements: If the global has been added to a module (ownership transferred), the caller must NOT delete it.
Cxt must not be used after deletion.

functions.name: WasmEdge_PluginLoadWithDefaultPaths
functions.description: Loads all WasmEdge plugins found in the default search locations (WASMEDGE_PLUGIN_PATH env var, the ../plugin/ directory relative to the WasmEdge install, and the wasmedge/ directory under the system library path for /usr installs). Use this before querying or instantiating plugins or their modules.
requirements: Must be called before attempting to find plugins or list modules using this API.
Has no parameters and no return value; callers cannot directly detect load failures via return code.
Loading locations are as documented; behavior depends on runtime environment (e.g., env var, install path).

functions.name: WasmEdge_PluginLoadFromPath
functions.description: Loads plugins from a caller-provided file or directory path. If Path is a file, loads that single plugin; if a directory, loads all plugins under it recursively.
requirements: Path must point to a readable plugin file or a directory containing plugins; otherwise no plugins will be loaded.
Call before querying or instantiating plugins or their modules.
No return value; callers must use other APIs (e.g., list/find) to observe results or detect absence of plugins.

functions.name: WasmEdge_PluginListPluginsLength
functions.description: Returns the count of currently loaded plugins.
requirements: Call after loading plugins via default paths or a specific path to get a meaningful count.

functions.name: WasmEdge_PluginListPlugins
functions.signature: WASMEDGE_CAPI_EXPORT extern uint32_t WasmEdge_PluginListPlugins(WasmEdge_String *Names, const uint32_t Len);
functions.description: Writes the names of loaded plugins into the provided Names array of length Len and returns the total number of loaded plugins. Names are owned by WasmEdge and must not be freed by the caller. If Len is smaller than the number of plugins, excess names are discarded.
requirements: Names must point to a writable array of WasmEdge_String with at least Len elements when Len > 0.
Len may be 0 to query the total size without writing output.
The WasmEdge_String values returned are owned by internal plugin storage; the caller must NOT call WasmEdge_StringDelete on them.
Should be called after plugins have been loaded to obtain valid entries.

functions.name: WasmEdge_PluginFind
functions.signature: WASMEDGE_CAPI_EXPORT extern const WasmEdge_PluginContext * WasmEdge_PluginFind(const WasmEdge_String Name);
functions.description: Finds and returns a pointer to a loaded plugin context by its name, or NULL if not found. Use the returned context to query modules or create module instances.
requirements: Name must be a valid WasmEdge_String representing the plugin name.
Call only after loading plugins via the provided loading APIs.
Caller must treat the returned context pointer as read-only and not attempt to free it.

functions.name: WasmEdge_PluginGetPluginName
functions.description: Returns the WasmEdge_String name associated with a plugin context. The returned string is owned by WasmEdge; do not delete it. Returns an empty string (Length 0, Buf NULL) on failure.
requirements: Cxt must be a valid pointer to a WasmEdge_PluginContext obtained from this API.
The returned string must NOT be freed with WasmEdge_StringDelete.

functions.name: WasmEdge_PluginListModuleLength
functions.description: Returns the number of modules available in the specified plugin context.
requirements: Cxt must be a valid pointer to a WasmEdge_PluginContext obtained from this API.
Call after loading plugins and obtaining the plugin context.

functions.name: WasmEdge_PluginListModule
functions.signature: WASMEDGE_CAPI_EXPORT extern uint32_t WasmEdge_PluginListModule(const WasmEdge_PluginContext *Cxt,                           WasmEdge_String *Names, const uint32_t Len);
functions.description: Writes module names from the given plugin context into Names (up to Len entries) and returns the total number of modules in the plugin. Names are owned by WasmEdge and must not be freed. Excess names are discarded if Len is smaller than the number of modules.
requirements: Cxt must be a valid pointer to a WasmEdge_PluginContext.
Names must point to a writable array of WasmEdge_String with at least Len elements when Len > 0.
Len may be 0 to query the total size without writing output.
The WasmEdge_String values returned are owned by internal plugin storage; the caller must NOT call WasmEdge_StringDelete on them.

functions.name: WasmEdge_PluginCreateModule
functions.signature: WASMEDGE_CAPI_EXPORT extern WasmEdge_ModuleInstanceContext * WasmEdge_PluginCreateModule(const WasmEdge_PluginContext *Cxt,                             const WasmEdge_String ModuleName);
functions.description: Creates and returns a module instance from the specified plugin by module name. Returns NULL if the module name is not found or the plugin is invalid. The caller owns the returned instance and must delete it when done.
requirements: Cxt must be a valid WasmEdge_PluginContext obtained via this API.
ModuleName must be a valid WasmEdge_String naming a module available in the plugin.
On success, the caller must destroy the returned module with WasmEdge_ModuleInstanceDelete.
Call only after the plugin providing the module has been loaded.

functions.name: WasmEdge_PluginInitWASINN
functions.signature: WASMEDGE_CAPI_EXPORT extern void WasmEdge_PluginInitWASINN(const char *const *NNPreloads,                           const uint32_t PreloadsLen);
functions.description: Initializes the wasi_nn plugin with an optional list of preload strings. Only valid after loading the wasi_nn plugin and before creating a module instance from it.
requirements: Must be called after the wasi_nn plugin has been loaded.
Must be called before creating any module instance from the wasi_nn plugin.
NNPreloads may be NULL if PreloadsLen is 0; otherwise it must point to an array of PreloadsLen C strings.
No return value; errors are not reported via return code.

functions.name: WasmEdge_Plugin_GetDescriptor
functions.description: Entry point implemented by a plugin to return its static plugin descriptor (name, description, API/semantic version, modules, and program options).
requirements: This function is implemented by plugins; hosts call it to obtain the descriptor.
Returns a pointer to plugin-owned data; callers must not free or modify the descriptor contents.

functions.name: WasmEdge_Driver_Compiler
functions.signature: WASMEDGE_CAPI_EXPORT extern int WasmEdge_Driver_Compiler(int Argc, const char *Argv[]);
functions.description: Entrypoint to run the WasmEdge AOT compiler tool from an embedding application using command-line style arguments. Pass the argument count and an array of C strings that represent the CLI options/operands the compiler expects. Returns an execution status suitable for use as a process exit code (0 typically means success; non‑zero indicates failure or specific status).
requirements: Argc must equal the number of elements supplied in Argv.
Argv must point to a valid array of Argc pointers to null-terminated C strings.
Strings in Argv are expected to be UTF-8 encoded (on Windows, use WasmEdge_Driver_ArgvCreate to convert UTF-16 to UTF-8).
Argv and all strings it references must remain valid for the duration of the call; the function does not take ownership.
Argc should be non-negative.
Callers should use the returned integer as an execution status/exit code and handle non-zero values as failures or tool-specific statuses.

functions.name: WasmEdge_Driver_Tool
functions.signature: WASMEDGE_CAPI_EXPORT extern int WasmEdge_Driver_Tool(int Argc, const char *Argv[]);
functions.description: Entrypoint to run the WasmEdge runtime tool with command-line style arguments. Provide the count and vector of option/value strings as if invoking the runtime from a shell. Returns an execution status suitable for use as a process exit code (0 typically means success; non‑zero indicates failure or specific status).
requirements: Argc must equal the number of elements supplied in Argv.
Argv must point to a valid array of Argc pointers to null-terminated C strings.
Strings in Argv are expected to be UTF-8 encoded (on Windows, use WasmEdge_Driver_ArgvCreate to convert UTF-16 to UTF-8).
Argv and all strings it references must remain valid for the duration of the call; the function does not take ownership.
Argc should be non-negative.
Callers should use the returned integer as an execution status/exit code and handle non-zero values as failures or tool-specific statuses.

functions.name: WasmEdge_Driver_UniTool
functions.signature: WASMEDGE_CAPI_EXPORT extern int WasmEdge_Driver_UniTool(int Argc, const char *Argv[]);
functions.description: Entrypoint to run the WasmEdge unified tool (a single binary providing multiple subcommands) using command-line style arguments. Supply the usual argc/argv pair that encodes the desired subcommand and options. Returns an execution status suitable for use as a process exit code (0 typically means success; non‑zero indicates failure or specific status).
requirements: Argc must equal the number of elements supplied in Argv.
Argv must point to a valid array of Argc pointers to null-terminated C strings.
Strings in Argv are expected to be UTF-8 encoded (on Windows, use WasmEdge_Driver_ArgvCreate to convert UTF-16 to UTF-8).
Argv and all strings it references must remain valid for the duration of the call; the function does not take ownership.
Argc should be non-negative.
Callers should use the returned integer as an execution status/exit code and handle non-zero values as failures or tool-specific statuses.

functions.name: WasmEdge_ValTypeGenI32
functions.description: Creates a WasmEdge_ValType representing the WASM I32 type. Use this when building function signatures or validating value types.
requirements: No input requirements; callable at any time.
The returned WasmEdge_ValType should be treated as an opaque value-type descriptor and used with other WasmEdge APIs.

functions.name: WasmEdge_ValTypeGenI64
functions.description: Creates a WasmEdge_ValType representing the WASM I64 type for use in signatures or type checks.
requirements: No input requirements; callable at any time.
Use the result only as a value-type descriptor with WasmEdge APIs.

functions.name: WasmEdge_ValTypeGenF32
functions.description: Creates a WasmEdge_ValType representing the WASM F32 type.
requirements: No input requirements; callable at any time.

functions.name: WasmEdge_ValTypeGenF64
functions.description: Creates a WasmEdge_ValType representing the WASM F64 type.
requirements: No input requirements; callable at any time.

functions.name: WasmEdge_ValTypeGenV128
functions.description: Creates a WasmEdge_ValType representing the WASM V128 SIMD type.
requirements: No input requirements; callable at any time.
Consumers should ensure SIMD/V128 is supported in their environment if required by other APIs (not enforced by this function).

functions.name: WasmEdge_ValTypeGenFuncRef
functions.description: Creates a WasmEdge_ValType representing the WASM funcref reference type.
requirements: No input requirements; callable at any time.
Useful only if the engine is configured with reference types support.

functions.name: WasmEdge_ValTypeGenExternRef
functions.description: Creates a WasmEdge_ValType representing the WASM externref reference type.
requirements: No input requirements; callable at any time.
Useful only if the engine is configured with reference types support.

functions.name: WasmEdge_ValTypeIsEqual
functions.signature: bool WasmEdge_ValTypeIsEqual(const WasmEdge_ValType ValType1, const WasmEdge_ValType ValType2);
functions.description: Compares two WasmEdge_ValType objects for equality of their encoded WASM value type.
requirements: ValType1 and ValType2 must be initialized WasmEdge_ValType objects (e.g., created via WasmEdge_ValTypeGen*).

functions.name: WasmEdge_ValTypeIsI32
functions.description: Returns whether the provided WasmEdge_ValType encodes the I32 type.
requirements: ValType should be a valid/initialized WasmEdge_ValType.

functions.name: WasmEdge_ValTypeIsI64
functions.description: Returns whether the provided WasmEdge_ValType encodes the I64 type.
requirements: ValType should be a valid/initialized WasmEdge_ValType.

functions.name: WasmEdge_ValTypeIsF32
functions.description: Returns whether the provided WasmEdge_ValType encodes the F32 type.
requirements: ValType should be a valid/initialized WasmEdge_ValType.

functions.name: WasmEdge_ValTypeIsF64
functions.description: Returns whether the provided WasmEdge_ValType encodes the F64 type.
requirements: ValType should be a valid/initialized WasmEdge_ValType.

functions.name: WasmEdge_ValTypeIsV128
functions.description: Returns whether the provided WasmEdge_ValType encodes the V128 type.
requirements: ValType should be a valid/initialized WasmEdge_ValType.

functions.name: WasmEdge_ValTypeIsFuncRef
functions.description: Returns whether the provided WasmEdge_ValType encodes the funcref type.
requirements: ValType should be a valid/initialized WasmEdge_ValType.

functions.name: WasmEdge_ValTypeIsExternRef
functions.description: Returns whether the provided WasmEdge_ValType encodes the externref type.
requirements: ValType should be a valid/initialized WasmEdge_ValType.

functions.name: WasmEdge_ValTypeIsRef
functions.description: Returns whether the provided WasmEdge_ValType encodes any reference type (nullable or non-nullable).
requirements: ValType should be a valid/initialized WasmEdge_ValType.

functions.name: WasmEdge_ValTypeIsRefNull
functions.description: Returns whether the provided WasmEdge_ValType encodes a nullable reference type.
requirements: ValType should be a valid/initialized WasmEdge_ValType.

functions.name: WasmEdge_ValueGenI32
functions.description: Constructs a WasmEdge_Value holding a 32-bit integer (I32). Typically used to build argument lists or results for WASM function calls.
requirements: Val must fit in a 32-bit signed integer (int32_t).
Use WasmEdge_ValueGetI32 to retrieve the stored value.

functions.name: WasmEdge_ValueGenI64
functions.description: Constructs a WasmEdge_Value holding a 64-bit integer (I64).
requirements: Val must fit in a 64-bit signed integer (int64_t).
Use WasmEdge_ValueGetI64 to retrieve the stored value.

functions.name: WasmEdge_ValueGenF32
functions.description: Constructs a WasmEdge_Value holding a 32-bit float (F32).
requirements: Val is a 32-bit IEEE-754 float.
Use WasmEdge_ValueGetF32 to retrieve the stored value.

functions.name: WasmEdge_ValueGenF64
functions.description: Constructs a WasmEdge_Value holding a 64-bit float (F64).
requirements: Val is a 64-bit IEEE-754 double.
Use WasmEdge_ValueGetF64 to retrieve the stored value.

functions.name: WasmEdge_ValueGenV128
functions.description: Constructs a WasmEdge_Value holding a 128-bit vector value (V128).
requirements: Val must be representable in int128_t.
Use WasmEdge_ValueGetV128 to retrieve the stored value.

functions.name: WasmEdge_ValueGenFuncRef
functions.description: Constructs a WasmEdge_Value holding a function reference (funcref) to the given function instance context. Only meaningful when the Bulk Memory Operations or Reference Types proposal is enabled in configuration.
requirements: Cxt should be a valid pointer to a WasmEdge_FunctionInstanceContext obtained from the runtime; unknown behavior if it does not refer to a live function instance.
Feature requirement: the engine/config must enable either WasmEdge_Proposal_BulkMemoryOperations or WasmEdge_Proposal_ReferenceTypes for the value to be meaningful.

functions.name: WasmEdge_ValueGenExternRef
functions.description: Constructs a WasmEdge_Value holding an external reference (externref) to an application object pointer. Only meaningful when the Reference Types proposal is enabled.
requirements: Ref is an arbitrary pointer managed by the host; lifetime/validity management is the caller’s responsibility (not enforced by this function).
Feature requirement: the engine/config must enable WasmEdge_Proposal_ReferenceTypes for the value to be meaningful.

functions.name: WasmEdge_ValueGetI32
functions.description: Extracts the 32-bit integer from a WasmEdge_Value previously constructed as an I32.
requirements: Val must contain an I32 (i.e., created by WasmEdge_ValueGenI32 or returned from an API producing I32). Using a value of another type is unspecified.
No side effects; safe to call multiple times.

functions.name: WasmEdge_ValueGetI64
functions.description: Extracts the 64-bit integer from a WasmEdge_Value previously constructed as an I64.
requirements: Val must contain an I64. Using a value of another type is unspecified.

functions.name: WasmEdge_ValueGetF32
functions.description: Extracts the 32-bit float from a WasmEdge_Value previously constructed as an F32.
requirements: Val must contain an F32. Using a value of another type is unspecified.

functions.name: WasmEdge_ValueGetF64
functions.description: Extracts the 64-bit float from a WasmEdge_Value previously constructed as an F64.
requirements: Val must contain an F64. Using a value of another type is unspecified.

functions.name: WasmEdge_ValueGetV128
functions.description: Extracts the 128-bit vector value from a WasmEdge_Value previously constructed as a V128.
requirements: Val must contain a V128. Using a value of another type is unspecified.

functions.name: WasmEdge_ValueIsNullRef
functions.description: Indicates whether the given WasmEdge_Value encodes a null reference.
requirements: Val should be a reference-typed value (funcref/externref) for the result to be meaningful; behavior for non-ref values is unspecified by this header.

functions.name: WasmEdge_ValueGetFuncRef
functions.description: Retrieves the function instance context pointer stored in a funcref WasmEdge_Value.
requirements: Val must contain a funcref (created via WasmEdge_ValueGenFuncRef or returned by APIs).
If Val is a null reference, the returned pointer may be NULL (not explicitly documented; treat as unknown).

functions.name: WasmEdge_ValueGetExternRef
functions.description: Retrieves the external reference pointer stored in an externref WasmEdge_Value.
requirements: Val must contain an externref (created via WasmEdge_ValueGenExternRef or returned by APIs).
If Val is a null reference, the returned pointer may be NULL (not explicitly documented; treat as unknown).

functions.name: WasmEdge_VMCreate
functions.signature: WASMEDGE_CAPI_EXPORT extern WasmEdge_VMContext * WasmEdge_VMCreate(const WasmEdge_ConfigureContext *ConfCxt, WasmEdge_StoreContext *StoreCxt);
functions.description: Create a new WasmEdge VM context with an optional configuration and optional external store. The caller owns the returned VM and must destroy it with WasmEdge_VMDelete. If StoreCxt is NULL, the VM owns an internal default store; otherwise, the provided store is used.
requirements: ConfCxt may be NULL to use default configuration.
StoreCxt may be NULL to use a VM-owned default store; if non-NULL, its lifetime must outlast the VM context.
On success returns a non-NULL pointer; NULL indicates failure and should be handled by the caller.
Caller must destroy the returned VM with WasmEdge_VMDelete when no longer needed.

functions.name: WasmEdge_VMRegisterModuleFromFile
functions.signature: WASMEDGE_CAPI_EXPORT extern WasmEdge_Result WasmEdge_VMRegisterModuleFromFile(WasmEdge_VMContext *Cxt, const WasmEdge_String ModuleName, const char *Path);
functions.description: Load a WASM module from a file, register all its exported instances into the VM store under the given module name, and instantiate them. Thread-safe.
requirements: Cxt must be a valid WasmEdge_VMContext.
ModuleName must specify the target module name to register exports under.
Path must be a valid NULL-terminated C string to a WASM file.
Check the returned WasmEdge_Result; use WasmEdge_ResultGetMessage for error details.

functions.name: WasmEdge_VMRegisterModuleFromBytes
functions.signature: WASMEDGE_CAPI_EXPORT extern WasmEdge_Result WasmEdge_VMRegisterModuleFromBytes(WasmEdge_VMContext *Cxt, const WasmEdge_String ModuleName, const WasmEdge_Bytes Bytes);
functions.description: Load a WASM module from an in-memory WasmEdge_Bytes, register all exported instances into the VM store under the given module name, and instantiate them. Thread-safe.
requirements: Cxt must be a valid WasmEdge_VMContext.
ModuleName must specify the target module name to register exports under.
Bytes must contain the WASM binary to load.
Check the returned WasmEdge_Result; use WasmEdge_ResultGetMessage for error details.

functions.name: WasmEdge_VMRegisterModuleFromASTModule
functions.signature: WASMEDGE_CAPI_EXPORT extern WasmEdge_Result WasmEdge_VMRegisterModuleFromASTModule(WasmEdge_VMContext *Cxt, const WasmEdge_String ModuleName, const WasmEdge_ASTModuleContext *ASTCxt);
functions.description: Register and instantiate a pre-loaded AST module into the VM store under the given module name, exposing all its exports. Thread-safe.
requirements: Cxt must be a valid WasmEdge_VMContext.
ModuleName must specify the target module name to register exports under.
ASTCxt must be a valid WasmEdge AST module context produced by loader or compiler.
Check the returned WasmEdge_Result; use WasmEdge_ResultGetMessage for error details.

functions.name: WasmEdge_VMRegisterModuleFromImport
functions.description: Register an existing module instance into the VM’s store using its module name, making its exports available for linking by other modules. Thread-safe.
requirements: Cxt must be a valid WasmEdge_VMContext.
ImportCxt must be a valid existing WasmEdge_ModuleInstanceContext to register.
The lifetime of ImportCxt must be guaranteed while it may be imported by other modules; using it after deletion can cause errors.
If the existing module instance will not be used anymore or after VM deletion, call WasmEdge_ModuleInstanceDelete; deletion will automatically unregister it from the VM store.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces a single bytes buffer intended to be consumed by
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR() and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() in the provided stubs. The
# data type is an arbitrary NULL-terminated UTF-8/byte string; the harness
# will split/consume as needed. We therefore craft a compact corpus container
# composed of multiple NUL-terminated strings concatenated, so each consumer
# can pick the next C-string. We keep them ASCII/UTF-8 friendly and include
# interesting values for WasmEdge tool/VM paths, names, and WASI argv/envs.
# The buffer does NOT exceed 4096 bytes.

_SAFE_ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_./:+=,[]{}()@#%\n "


def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Avoid embedded NULs; stick to safe ASCII and spaces/newlines
    return "".join(rng.choice(_SAFE_ASCII) for _ in range(n)).strip("\0") or "a"


def _toolish_args(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Mix of realistic flags and placeholders; include names for funcs/modules.
    flags_pool = [
        "--opt-level=0", "--opt-level=3", "-o", "--dump-ir", "--generic-binary",
        "--interruptible", "--allow-afunix", "--reactor",
        "--func=main", "--func=_start", "--func=add",
        "--cfg=default", "--enable=simd", "--disable=simd",
    ]
    args: List[str] = []
    # Tool name first (program name)
    args.append(rng.choice(["wasmedge", "wasmedgec", "wasmedge-unified"]))
    # A few flags
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4)):
        args.append(rng.choice(flags_pool))
    # Add a plausible function/module name sometimes
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        args.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 3, 12))
    return args


def _wasi_envs(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    envs = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)):
        k = _rand_ascii(rng, 3, 8).replace("=", "_")
        v = _rand_ascii(rng, 0, 10)
        envs.append(f"{k}={v}")
    return envs


def _wasi_preopens(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Preopens can be "GUEST:HOST" or a single path
    res = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)):
        guest = "/" + _rand_ascii(rng, 3, 8).replace(" ", "_")
        host = "/" + _rand_ascii(rng, 3, 8).replace(" ", "_")
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            res.append(f"{guest}:{host}")
        else:
            res.append(host)
    return res


def _paths(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Some plausible wasm and output paths; harness will pick any as C-strings
    base = "/tmp/" if rng.random() < 0.7 else "./"
    wasm_names = [
        "mod.wasm", "test.wasm", "a.wasm", _rand_ascii(rng, 3, 8) + ".wasm"
    ]
    out_names = [
        "out.so", "out.aot", "out", _rand_ascii(rng, 3, 8)
    ]
    paths = [base + rng.choice(wasm_names), base + rng.choice(out_names)]
    # Also include a couple arbitrary file-ish strings
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 2)):
        paths.append(base + _rand_ascii(rng, 3, 10))
    return paths


def _module_and_func_names(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    names = []
    # Small set of likely export names and random ones
    names += ["_start", "main", "add", "run", "memory", "table"]
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
        names.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 3, 12))
    return names


def _wasm_minimal_module() -> bytes:
    # A smallest valid wasm module in binary form (no functions). For our string
    # corpus, embed it as a hex string label and as filename is handled elsewhere.
    # However, stubs expect C-strings, so we only include textual tokens; the
    # actual bytes for WasmEdge_Bytes are sourced from FUZZ_PARAM_STR(), which will
    # read our NUL-separated chunks as raw bytes. Include a chunk that is the real
    # wasm magic+version so some calls see valid prefix.
    return b"\x00asm\x01\x00\x00\x00"


def _nn_preloads(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Preloads for wasi-nn; any strings are acceptable
    opts = ["openvino", "pytorch", "tensorflow", "onnx"]
    res = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)):
        res.append(rng.choice(opts))
    return res


def _to_corpus(strings: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # Join as NUL-terminated C-strings; ensure final ends with NUL as well
    data = b"\x00".join(s for s in strings) + b"\x00"
    return data[:4096]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    chunks: List[bytes] = []

    # Tool-like argv sets
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        for s in _toolish_args(rng):
            chunks.append(s.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore"))

    # WASI argv/envs/preopens
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 2)):
        for s in _wasi_envs(rng):
            chunks.append(s.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore"))
        for s in _wasi_preopens(rng):
            chunks.append(s.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore"))

    # Paths and filenames for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME users
    for p in _paths(rng):
        chunks.append(p.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore"))

    # Module and function names
    for n in _module_and_func_names(rng):
        chunks.append(n.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore"))

    # Include several arbitrary strings of varying lengths (including empty)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        chunks.append(b"")
    for _ in range(rng.randint(4, 10)):
        chunks.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 1, 64).encode("utf-8", errors="ignore"))

    # Include a valid wasm header prefix chunk to increase success rate
    chunks.append(_wasm_minimal_module())

    # A couple of likely option/value pairs used by drivers
    driver_pairs = ["-o", "/tmp/out.aot", "--func", "_start", "--func", "main"]
    for s in driver_pairs:
        chunks.append(s.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore"))

    # Ensure total size under limit
    corpus = _to_corpus(chunks)
    return corpus

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator produces valid and interesting arbitrary byte buffers aimed at
# exercising WasmEdge APIs that accept byte views (WasmEdge_String*, WasmEdge_Bytes,
# and WASM binary buffers). It focuses on producing:
# - UTF-8-like text of varying sizes (for String* paths)
# - Null-inclusive byte arrays (to ensure explicit-length behavior is tested)
# - Valid minimal WebAssembly binaries (to drive paths that require valid WASM)
# - Slight variants of valid WASM (still valid but different sections/order/size)
# - Repeated patterns and random bytes
# Buffer size is limited to <= 4096 bytes as requested.

# Minimal valid WASM module: (module)
# Magic: 0x00 61 73 6d, Version: 0x01 00 00 00
# Empty module has no sections, but many engines require at least an empty code.
# However, a minimal valid module with no sections is valid per spec.
WASM_MAGIC = b"\x00asm"  # 00 61 73 6d
WASM_VERSION_1 = b"\x01\x00\x00\x00"

# Helper: LEB128 unsigned encoder for small values
def _u32_leb(x: int) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    v = x & 0xFFFFFFFF
    while True:
        b = v & 0x7F
        v >>= 7
        if v:
            out.append(b | 0x80)
        else:
            out.append(b)
            break
    return bytes(out)

# Create a small but valid wasm with an exported function that returns i32 const
# (func (export "f") (result i32) i32.const 42)
# Sections: type, func, export, code
def _wasm_simple_add(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Type section (id=1)
    # one type: func type: params N, results M
    # For diversity, choose 0-2 params of i32 and 0-1 result
    nparams = rng.choice([0, 1, 2])
    params = b"".join([b"\x7f" for _ in range(nparams)])  # 0x7F = i32
    nresults = rng.choice([0, 1])
    results = b"" if nresults == 0 else b"\x7f"
    functype = b"\x60" + _u32_leb(nparams) + params + _u32_leb(nresults) + results
    type_section_payload = _u32_leb(1) + functype
    type_section = b"\x01" + _u32_leb(len(type_section_payload)) + type_section_payload

    # Function section (id=3) -> 1 function referring to type 0
    func_sec_payload = _u32_leb(1) + _u32_leb(0)
    func_section = b"\x03" + _u32_leb(len(func_sec_payload)) + func_sec_payload

    # Export section (id=7) -> export one function named "f"
    name = b"f"
    export_desc_func = b"\x00" + _u32_leb(0)  # kind func, index 0
    export_entry = _u32_leb(len(name)) + name + export_desc_func
    export_payload = _u32_leb(1) + export_entry
    export_section = b"\x07" + _u32_leb(len(export_payload)) + export_payload

    # Code section (id=10) -> 1 body
    # body: locals vec (0), then instructions. We'll ensure valid end opcode 0x0b
    # choose instruction sequence depending on nresults
    body_instr = bytearray()
    if nresults == 0:
        # no result: empty function body
        pass
    else:
        # push a small constant result
        val = rng.randint(0, 100)
        body_instr += b"\x41" + _u32_leb(val)  # i32.const
    body_instr += b"\x0b"  # end
    locals_vec = _u32_leb(0)
    func_body = locals_vec + bytes(body_instr)
    body_size = _u32_leb(len(func_body))
    code_payload = _u32_leb(1) + body_size + func_body
    code_section = b"\x0a" + _u32_leb(len(code_payload)) + code_payload

    wasm = WASM_MAGIC + WASM_VERSION_1 + type_section + func_section + export_section + code_section
    return wasm

# Minimal empty module (valid per spec): magic+version only
def _wasm_empty() -> bytes:
    return WASM_MAGIC + WASM_VERSION_1

# WASM with data section and memory to test memory/table related code paths
# (module (memory 1) (data (i32.const 0) "abc"))
# Sections: type (empty), memory, data
def _wasm_memory_data() -> bytes:
    # Memory section (id=5)
    # vec(memory): count=1, memtype: limits flags=0x00 (min only), min=1
    memtype = b"\x00" + _u32_leb(1)
    mem_payload = _u32_leb(1) + memtype
    mem_section = b"\x05" + _u32_leb(len(mem_payload)) + mem_payload

    # Data section (id=11)
    # vec(data): 1 segment, active: 0x00, expr: i32.const 0x00, end 0x0b, init bytes "abc"
    init = b"abc"
    expr = b"\x41\x00\x0b"
    seg = b"\x00" + expr + _u32_leb(len(init)) + init
    data_payload = _u32_leb(1) + seg
    data_section = b"\x0b" + _u32_leb(len(data_payload)) + data_payload

    return WASM_MAGIC + WASM_VERSION_1 + mem_section + data_section

# Text builders for WasmEdge_String consumers
ASCII_WORDS = [
    b"hello", b"world", b"wasmedge", b"module", b"_start", b"main", b"func", b"memory",
    b"export", b"import", b"table", b"global", b"verylongmodulename", b"wasi", b"plugin",
]

UNICODE_FRAGMENTS = [
    "αβγ", "漢字", "🙂", "🚀", "функция", "テスト", "مرحبا", "ąćęłńóśźż",
]

def _rand_utf8(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    while sum(len(p) for p in parts) < target_len:
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            parts.append(rng.choice(ASCII_WORDS))
            if rng.random() < 0.3:
                parts.append(b"\x00")  # embed NUL to test explicit length handling
        else:
            parts.append(rng.choice(UNICODE_FRAGMENTS).encode("utf-8"))
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            parts.append(b"-")
    out = b"".join(parts)
    return out[:target_len]

def _random_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Bias towards 0x00, 0xFF, ASCII, and random
    out = bytearray()
    for i in range(n):
        p = rng.random()
        if p < 0.15:
            out.append(0)
        elif p < 0.25:
            out.append(0xFF)
        elif p < 0.6:
            out.append(rng.randrange(32, 127))
        else:
            out.append(rng.randrange(256))
    return bytes(out)

# Compose several strategies and pick based on seed

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide an overarching scenario
    scenario = rng.choices(
        population=[
            "valid_wasm_empty",
            "valid_wasm_simple",
            "valid_wasm_memory",
            "utf8_text_short",
            "utf8_text_long",
            "random_bytes_small",
            "random_bytes_medium",
            "repeated_pattern",
        ],
        weights=[10, 30, 15, 8, 7, 10, 8, 12],
        k=1,
    )[0]

    max_total = 4096

    if scenario == "valid_wasm_empty":
        return _wasm_empty()

    if scenario == "valid_wasm_simple":
        return _wasm_simple_add(seed ^ 0xA5A5)

    if scenario == "valid_wasm_memory":
        return _wasm_memory_data()

    if scenario == "utf8_text_short":
        length = rng.randint(1, 128)
        return _rand_utf8(rng, length)

    if scenario == "utf8_text_long":
        length = rng.randint(256, 2048)
        return _rand_utf8(rng, length)

    if scenario == "random_bytes_small":
        n = rng.randint(1, 256)
        return _random_bytes(rng, n)

    if scenario == "random_bytes_medium":
        n = rng.randint(512, 2048)
        return _random_bytes(rng, n)

    if scenario == "repeated_pattern":
        # Build repeated sequences including zeros and ASCII to test StringCopy and wrap lengths
        base_choices = [b"A", b"\x00", b"xyz", b"1234", b"\xff\x00", b"name:"]
        pattern = b"".join(rng.choices(base_choices, k=rng.randint(2, 8)))
        reps = max(1, rng.randint(1, max_total // max(1, len(pattern))))
        data = (pattern * reps)[:rng.randint(32, min(3072, len(pattern) * reps))]
        return data

    # Fallback (should not hit): random bytes
    return _random_bytes(rng, rng.randint(1, 512))

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for valid filesystem path strings to feed FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME and FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# Target usage:
# - FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME: must reference an existing file with random data
# - FUZZ_PARAM_STR: used as arbitrary strings (argv tokens, module names), but sometimes filenames too
# Our strategy:
# 1) Create a small in-memory virtual file layout in the temp directory for the fuzz run.
# 2) Return a bytes object containing a newline-separated list of candidate paths and tokens.
#    The harness will pull from this buffer to create files as needed; but since FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME
#    requires an existing file, we proactively create files and directories and return their paths.
# 3) Ensure paths are NUL-terminated when interpreted as C strings by including only ASCII and avoiding NULs.
# 4) Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

# We emit a corpus that mixes:
# - Valid WASM magic files (\0asm + version) to increase chances of successful parsing/compilation
# - Random binary files of various sizes (including empty)
# - Paths with special characters, spaces, dots, long components, nested directories
# - Distinct temporary files to reduce collisions between input and output paths

MAGIC_WASM = b"\x00asm\x01\x00\x00\x00"  # WebAssembly binary header (version 1)

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_. "


def _rand_name(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 3, max_len: int = 12, allow_spaces: bool = True) -> str:
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    chars = SAFE_CHARS if allow_spaces else (string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_.")
    return ''.join(rng.choice(chars) for _ in range(length)).strip() or "x"


def _ensure_dir(path: str) -> None:
    try:
        os.makedirs(path, exist_ok=True)
    except Exception:
        pass


def _write_file(path: str, data: bytes) -> None:
    try:
        # Ensure parent exists
        parent = os.path.dirname(path)
        if parent:
            _ensure_dir(parent)
        with open(path, 'wb') as f:
            f.write(data)
    except Exception:
        # Best-effort; if writing fails, leave it (the path may still exist or another will work)
        pass


def _make_wasm_like(rng: random.Random, max_extra: int = 128) -> bytes:
    # Construct a minimal wasm-like buffer: header + some random bytes
    extra = rng.randint(0, max_extra)
    return MAGIC_WASM + rng.randbytes(extra)


def _make_random_bytes(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 1024) -> bytes:
    n = rng.randint(0, max_len)
    return rng.randbytes(n)


def _unique_path(rng: random.Random, base_dir: str, prefix: str = "", suffix: str = "") -> str:
    name = f"{prefix}{_rand_name(rng)}{suffix}"
    return os.path.join(base_dir, name)


def _build_corpus(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    paths: List[str] = []

    # Base temp directory for this seed to avoid collisions across runs
    base = os.path.join(
        os.path.abspath(os.getenv('TMPDIR') or os.getenv('TEMP') or '/tmp'),
        f"wasmedge_fuzz_{rng.getrandbits(32):08x}"
    )
    _ensure_dir(base)

    # Create nested directories
    nested_dirs = [
        os.path.join(base, "subdir"),
        os.path.join(base, "subdir with space"),
        os.path.join(base, ".hidden"),
        os.path.join(base, "a" * 10, "b" * 10),
    ]
    for d in nested_dirs:
        _ensure_dir(d)
        paths.append(d)

    # Create several files:
    # 1) Valid wasm-like files
    for i in range(3):
        p = _unique_path(rng, base, prefix=f"mod{i}_", suffix=".wasm")
        _write_file(p, _make_wasm_like(rng, max_extra=256))
        paths.append(p)

    # 2) Random binaries including empty
    rb_sizes = [0, 1, 8, 64, 512, 2048]
    for sz in rb_sizes:
        p = _unique_path(rng, base, prefix=f"bin{sz}_", suffix=".bin")
        data = (b"" if sz == 0 else rng.randbytes(sz))
        _write_file(p, data)
        paths.append(p)

    # 3) Files in nested dirs
    for d in nested_dirs:
        p = os.path.join(d, _rand_name(rng, allow_spaces=True) + ".dat")
        _write_file(p, _make_random_bytes(rng, max_len=300))
        paths.append(p)

    # 4) Another wasm-like with minimal content
    p_min = _unique_path(rng, base, prefix="minimal_", suffix=".wasm")
    _write_file(p_min, MAGIC_WASM)
    paths.append(p_min)

    # 5) A very long filename
    long_comp = _rand_name(rng, min_len=40, max_len=80, allow_spaces=False)
    p_long = os.path.join(base, long_comp + ".bin")
    _write_file(p_long, _make_random_bytes(rng, max_len=128))
    paths.append(p_long)

    # 6) Directory paths that might be passed to PluginLoadFromPath
    paths.extend(nested_dirs)

    # Add some relative paths
    rel1 = os.path.relpath(paths[0], start=base)
    rel2 = os.path.relpath(paths[-1], start=base)
    # Prepend base to ensure they are usable from any CWD via join; but also include raw relative
    paths.append(os.path.join(base, rel1))
    paths.append(rel2)

    # Ensure uniqueness and reasonable ordering
    uniq = []
    seen = set()
    for p in paths:
        if p not in seen:
            seen.add(p)
            uniq.append(p)

    return uniq


def _build_tokens(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Tokens for argv/module names etc.
    tokens: List[str] = [
        "wasmedgec", "wasmedge", "wasmedge-unified",
        "--help", "-v", "--optimize", "--dump-ir", "--generic-binary",
        "run", "compile", "--dir=/", "--enable-simd",
    ]
    # Add random ASCII tokens
    for _ in range(10):
        tokens.append(_rand_name(rng, min_len=1, max_len=16, allow_spaces=True))
    return tokens


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    paths = _build_corpus(rng)
    tokens = _build_tokens(rng)

    # Mix paths and tokens; FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME expects existing files, so we keep many file paths first
    lines: List[str] = []

    # Place several file paths up front to satisfy early filename requests
    lines.extend(paths)

    # Add tokens and also duplicate some paths to increase chance of distinct InPath/OutPath pairs
    extra = rng.sample(paths, k=min(len(paths), 10)) if paths else []
    lines.extend(tokens)
    lines.extend(extra)

    # Ensure newline-separated and within 4096 bytes
    blob = ("\n".join(lines) + "\n").encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    if len(blob) > 4096:
        # Trim conservatively
        blob = blob[:4096]
        # Ensure it ends with a newline to avoid partial path merge
        if not blob.endswith(b"\n"):
            last_nl = blob.rfind(b"\n")
            blob = blob[: last_nl + 1] if last_nl >= 0 else b"\n"

    return blob

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# We generate valid, interesting inputs for fuzz stubs that use FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME and FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
# The primary consumer here is WasmEdge_*FromFile / *CompilerCompile which expect a filename that exists
# and contains bytes that are often a valid WebAssembly module to exercise deeper paths. We therefore
# emit a single bytes buffer which the harness will materialize as a file. We pack multiple files in one
# buffer using a simple archive format so the harness can pick any FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME and still get
# an existing file with content. We include several variants:
# - A minimal valid WASM module (no imports/exports)
# - A module exporting a function named "_start" (for tools execution paths)
# - A module with name/exports to hit listing/lookup paths
# - A non-wasm random file to exercise error handling
# - A plausible plugin-like file name entry (content arbitrary)
#
# We also embed a small set of ASCII argument-like strings to be used by FUZZ_PARAM_STR call sites
# (driver tools). The harness typically draws FUZZ_PARAM_STR from the same input bytes.
#
# Container layout (little endian):
# magic: 8 bytes: b"WEDGEARC"
# u32: file_count (N)
# For each file i in [0..N):
#   u16: name_len
#   name bytes (ASCII, no NUL)
#   u32: content_len
#   content bytes
# u32: arg_count (M)
# For each arg j in [0..M):
#   u16: arg_len
#   arg bytes (ASCII)
# Total size <= 4096 bytes.

def _leb_u32(n: int) -> bytes:
    # Unsigned LEB128 encoding for small values
    out = bytearray()
    while True:
        byte = n & 0x7F
        n >>= 7
        if n:
            out.append(byte | 0x80)
        else:
            out.append(byte)
            break
    return bytes(out)

# Build minimal valid wasm modules
# 1) Empty module: 00 61 73 6D 01 00 00 00
_EMPTY_WASM = b"\x00asm\x01\x00\x00\x00"

# 2) Module exporting a function named _start that does nothing (func 0 with empty type)
# Sections:
# Type: 1 entry (func type [] -> [])
# Function: 1 func of type 0
# Export: export name "_start" func idx 0
# Code: 1 body: locals 0, body (end)

def _wasm_export_start() -> bytes:
    mod = bytearray(_EMPTY_WASM)
    # Type section id 1
    type_payload = bytearray()
    type_payload += _leb_u32(1)  # 1 type
    type_payload += b"\x60"      # func form
    type_payload += _leb_u32(0)  # param count 0
    type_payload += _leb_u32(0)  # result count 0
    type_sec = bytes([1]) + _leb_u32(len(type_payload)) + type_payload

    # Function section id 3
    func_payload = _leb_u32(1) + _leb_u32(0)  # 1 func, type idx 0
    func_sec = bytes([3]) + _leb_u32(len(func_payload)) + func_payload

    # Export section id 7
    name = b"_start"
    exp_payload = bytearray()
    exp_payload += _leb_u32(1)           # 1 export
    exp_payload += _leb_u32(len(name)) + name
    exp_payload += b"\x00"               # kind: func
    exp_payload += _leb_u32(0)           # func index 0
    exp_sec = bytes([7]) + _leb_u32(len(exp_payload)) + exp_payload

    # Code section id 10
    body = bytearray()
    body += _leb_u32(0)  # local decl count
    body += b"\x0b"     # end
    code_entry = _leb_u32(len(body)) + body
    code_payload = _leb_u32(1) + code_entry
    code_sec = bytes([10]) + _leb_u32(len(code_payload)) + code_payload

    mod += type_sec + func_sec + exp_sec + code_sec
    return bytes(mod)

# 3) Module exporting a named function "add" that returns i32.const 0, to exercise name handling
# Type: []->i32, function, export name "add", code pushing 0 and end

def _wasm_export_add() -> bytes:
    mod = bytearray(_EMPTY_WASM)
    # Type: 1 func []-> [i32]
    payload = bytearray()
    payload += _leb_u32(1)
    payload += b"\x60"           # func
    payload += _leb_u32(0)       # params 0
    payload += _leb_u32(1) + b"\x7f"  # results 1, i32
    type_sec = bytes([1]) + _leb_u32(len(payload)) + payload

    # Func
    func_payload = _leb_u32(1) + _leb_u32(0)
    func_sec = bytes([3]) + _leb_u32(len(func_payload)) + func_payload

    # Export
    name = b"add"
    exp_payload = bytearray()
    exp_payload += _leb_u32(1)
    exp_payload += _leb_u32(len(name)) + name
    exp_payload += b"\x00"  # func
    exp_payload += _leb_u32(0)
    exp_sec = bytes([7]) + _leb_u32(len(exp_payload)) + exp_payload

    # Code: locals 0, i32.const 0 (0x41 0x00), end (0x0b)
    body = bytearray()
    body += _leb_u32(0)
    body += b"\x41\x00\x0b"
    code_entry = _leb_u32(len(body)) + body
    code_payload = _leb_u32(1) + code_entry
    code_sec = bytes([10]) + _leb_u32(len(code_payload)) + code_payload

    mod += type_sec + func_sec + exp_sec + code_sec
    return bytes(mod)

# Random non-wasm content to trigger error paths

def _random_blob(rng: random.Random, size: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(size))

# Build argument strings relevant for WasmEdge drivers/tools

def _arg_strings(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    base = [
        "--help",
        "-h",
        "--opt-level=3",
        "--enable-simd",
        "--enable-threads",
        "--reactor",
        "run",
        "compile",
        "--dump-ir",
        "--generic-binary",
        "--wasm",
        "_start",
        "add",
    ]
    # Add a couple of randomized short ASCII tokens
    for _ in range(5):
        n = rng.randint(1, 12)
        s = ''.join(chr(rng.randint(0x61, 0x7a)) for _ in range(n))
        base.append(s)
    rng.shuffle(base)
    # Limit count to keep total size small
    return base[:12]

# Helper to package archive

def _pack_archive(files: List[tuple], args: List[str]) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    out += b"WEDGEARC"
    out += struct.pack('<I', len(files))
    for name, content in files:
        name_b = name.encode('ascii', 'ignore')[:255]
        out += struct.pack('<H', len(name_b))
        out += name_b
        out += struct.pack('<I', len(content))
        out += content
    out += struct.pack('<I', len(args))
    for a in args:
        ab = a.encode('ascii', 'ignore')[:255]
        out += struct.pack('<H', len(ab))
        out += ab
    return bytes(out)

# Public API

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Construct files
    files: List[tuple] = []

    # Minimal valid wasm
    files.append(("mod_empty.wasm", _EMPTY_WASM))
    # Exporting _start
    files.append(("mod_start.wasm", _wasm_export_start()))
    # Exporting add
    files.append(("mod_add.wasm", _wasm_export_add()))

    # Random invalid file to exercise error branches
    inv_size = rng.randint(16, 128)
    files.append(("random.bin", _random_blob(rng, inv_size)))

    # A file with .so extension to exercise PluginLoadFromPath code path (content arbitrary)
    plug_size = rng.randint(32, 96)
    files.append(("fake_plugin.so", _random_blob(rng, plug_size)))

    # Optionally include a larger but still bounded wasm by repeating a valid module with padding
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        padded = _wasm_export_add() + b"\x00" * rng.randint(0, 64)
        files.append(("padded.wasm", padded))

    # Build argument strings
    args = _arg_strings(rng)

    blob = _pack_archive(files, args)

    # Ensure size limit
    return blob[:4096]
